- Channel 1 (moving objects): strong structure only in rows 2â7, columns 1â8. Examples: (r3,c2)=7.09, (r3,c6)=7.19, (r6,c4)=5.44, (r6,c8)=5.45. Rows 1 and 8 are near baseline (~0.3â0.4). This suggests moving objects occupy a set of middle lanes, not the top or bottom rows.  
- Channel 2 (reward targets): almost all mass is on row 1, all columns: (r1,c1)=1.37, (r1,c2)=1.38, (r1,c3)=1.34, (r1,c4)=1.36, (r1,c5)=1.36, (r1,c6)=1.30, (r1,c7)=1.20, (r1,c8)=1.25. Other rows are ~0.3â0.4. This strongly indicates the reward/goal is the entire top row.  
- Channel 3 (obstacles): high only on the outer border, e.g. row 0, row 9, column 0, column 9 all ~1.2â1.35; interior mostly low. So only the wall border is an obstacle.  
- Channel 4 (previous frame): large norms in many playable cells, e.g. (r5,c2)=8.33, (r4,c7)=8.14, (r3,c1)=6.30, (r3,c8)=7.10, (r8,c5)=6.91. This is consistent with tracking previous agent/moving-object positions.

Reasoning:  
The channel layout matches a MinAtar-style grid game. The key clues are channel 2 and channel 1. Channel 2 being active only on the top row means the reward target is the top edge. Channel 1 being active only in rows 2â7 means the moving objects occupy middle lanes, not the top goal row or bottom start row. Channel 0 shows a 2D-moving agent that can be in many playable cells. This rules out Breakout (paddle at bottom, bricks in multiple top rows), Space Invaders (ship at bottom, aliens in multiple top rows, shields), Seaquest (fish/rewards throughout), and Asterix (objects throughout). It fits Freeway: a chicken starts at the bottom, cars move horizontally in middle lanes, and the goal is to reach the top row.

Game: Freeway (Atari Freeway / MinAtar Freeway).

Description: The agent controls a chicken crossing a multi-lane road, avoiding horizontally moving cars, and receives reward for reaching the top row.

Confidence: 95%
